text_fidelity_a:
(2023 Version) SkatingSpirit Slim Padded Figure Skating Shorts, Hip Tailbone Gel Pad Protective Underwear I usually wear a small in womens, but ordered up to a Medium. It fit like a toddler size. In other words, it did not come close to fitting. So I sized up to an XL and ordered again. It fit. But sadly, the padding -- which I saw on the Medium and fervently hoped would be bigger on the XL -- was still child sized. Adults have more surface area to fall on. These pads were narrow and small, targeting very small areas that one can easily miss during a fall. Also, I barely felt cushioned when I tried gently bumping my tailbone. The hips I didn't feel the padding on at all because I missed no matter how many times I tried falling while aiming for the padding.

The pads' holes are a smart idea to reduce weight, and the idea of breathable cotton shorts with packets sewn on for gel padding is a great idea that gets rid of the hassle of placing akton gel on each spot e.g. the famous skatingsafe gel gear that must be held in place with stinky synthetic tights. But unlike the akton gel, these gel pads, while squishy when pushed with a finger, don't seem to provide the same shock absorption. For now, I will stick to my puffy foam shorts as they provide more noticeabpe protection. I hope this company improves their design and I'd be the first to come back.
text_fidelity_b: (2023 Version) SkatingSpirit Slim Padded Figure Skating Shorts, Hip Tailbone Gel Pad Protective Underwear

text_fidelity_a:
VAULTEK VS20i Biometric Handgun Bluetooth 2.0 Smart Safe Pistol Safe with Auto-Open Lid and Rechargeable Battery (Biometric) The main issue I'm experiencing with this safe is the biometric scanner. The scanner recognizes my index finger print only 20% or less. The fail rate is unacceptable! I tried resetting/ erasing my finger prints and trying again to have the safe save my prints. I made sure the scanner was clean and my fingers were clean before re-doing the finger print save process. Also, I made sure each print saved was at a slightly different angle/ position to increase chances of the biometric scanner reading my prints correctly. Unfortunately, the fail rate was still very high at over 60% fail rate. It was able to recognize two fingers almost consistently, but not to the point where I would trust it to be my main point of access option in an emergency situation. I would rather use the keypad PIN or keys for emergency accesss. I'm considering the VT20 that doesn't include the biometric scanner or trying another VT20i an see if this first one is just defective or not. The other minor issue is that the interior lining inside the safe is not flush on all sides and sticks out a little at the top of mine where the hinge is located. The last minor issue is the battery removal method using a thin string that you pull on to remove the battery. If this string were to break or the user accidentally forgets to push the battery into the battery compartment with string first then it'll be difficult to remove the battery for replacement. The user manual doesn't state anything about the string at all. It seems like a cheap and ineffective battery removal process that can lead to issues in the future. Without the string in place behind the battery it is difficult to remove the battery because it sits flush into the battery compartment with little room to try to remove it with your fingers. This unit does use a rechargeable battery, but eventually it does require a battery replacement once the battery fails or the user wants to get a higher capacity rechargeable battery.
The overall construction of the safe seems sturdy and well built. During my testing I stored a Sig P226 handgun with a Streamlight TLR-4 attached and four 10 round magazines inside the safe (one mag was in the gun). The fitment was tight, but I was able to close the safe. The Andriod app for the Vaultek safe worked well, but I wish there was an option to secure the app with a PIN code instead of only a pattern lock. The app is straightforward and easy to use. The ability to view a history log of how the safe was accessed, whose finger print was used for access if biometric scanner was used, the battery level, turn sound on/off, adjust interior light, and open the safe from the app is great. The safe does make a distinct opening sound that is audible to anyone within the same room and the lid opens 90 degrees automatically when opened. The keypad does light up when you use it, which is a nice feature.
I'm disappointed one of the biggest selling features of this safe, the Biometric scanner, didn't work as advertised and had such a high fail rate in my experience. I'll try one more VT20i and report my results.
text_fidelity_b: VAULTEK VS20i Biometric Handgun Bluetooth 2.0 Smart Safe Pistol Safe with Auto-Open Lid and Rechargeable Battery (Biometric)

Sabre Tactical Pepper Gel with Belt Holster for Easy Carry, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Quick Access Flip Top Safety, Tactical Design for Security Professionals, 18 Bursts, 18-Foot Range Every method of self-defense involves a level of awareness and confidence. Exercising "situational awareness" will often allow you to avoid placing yourself in a position where you have to protect yourself. Escape of course is the second option assuming that there is an effective way to avoid a confrontation. But if you are finally forced to bring your use of force to the situation, you must be confident of your method and how to effectively deploy it.

Many years ago I tested a Sabre product for effectiveness. Having a wife and two young daughters motivated me to find something legal that they could carry and use properly without hurting themselves in the process. The particular Sabre unit I tested DID NOT PERFORM AS ADVERTISED! I wrote a poor product review and explained why I came to that conclusion. Unfortunately my review was targeted by numerous individuals who trashed my reasoning and perspective. Yes, the Sabre products have an outstanding reputation. But not every individual unit will work as promised!

About 35 years ago I worked as a product development manager for a company lastly known as We Care America -- formerly Weapons Corporation of America (WCA). One of the products we brought to market was a pepper spray intended for self-defense use. I couldn't put my name on the recommendation until I satisfied myself as to its effectiveness. That meant that I had to be sprayed in the face. Many law enforcement organizations require their officers to be sprayed so that they understand the proper use and deployment of their spray -- and so they know what their targeted individuals will go through.

My suggestion to you is to take your unit outside the house, find an area that is not windy, hold your off-hand away from you with the palm down, and spray the back of your hand a quick burst. You should feel sharp pain on the back of your hand. If you don't, you have a defective unit. If you do, simply wash off with soap and warm water. DO NOT PUT YOUR HANDS NEAR YOUR EYES!

A unit failure can be caused by a short expiration date, poor storage, or less than optimal shipping conditions. Even on this product page Sabre states that other brands experience a 30% failure rate (University of Utah study). If your unit produces the desired irritation, shoot a full burst away from you to get an idea of how well your can is pressurized. Your spray may not go the promised 18 feet. Be aware of its particular limitations. In any event, return it immediately if it doesn't perform as advertised.

Once you determine that your individual unit is effective, make sure to view the offered free training video and then practice deploying your unit without actually spraying it. You must have confidence in both your individual unit and in yourself. Practice may seem redundant but it can be a life saver.
text_fidelity_b: Sabre Tactical Pepper Gel with Belt Holster for Easy Carry, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Quick Access Flip Top Safety, Tactical Design for Security Professionals, 18 Bursts, 18-Foot Range

three major areas where this mat really shows it’s quality: 1) the grippiness – on the cheaper mats, it’s
easier for your fingers and foot to slide in positions like downward dog. This keeps you in place. 2) the
quality of the material – on the cheaper matters, when you do a position like downward dog, you
literally see the mat stretch – this is rigid. 3) the thickness – on the cheaper mats, doing things like cat
stretch hurt my knees – this has enough padding where it’s much more bearable.

The only downside for this mat, is it does get kind of dirty easily. But hey look, it's proof of the work put in. In short, a great mat – good balance of cost and quality.

text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Zip Wireless Activity Tracker, Magenta This is the third Fitbit device I have had and they all have gone bad in a very short time.  In the past I had a Fitbit One and a Fitbit Flex.  I have had this one just a few days over a month and have had a multitude of problems.  The first was that the display went blank.  When I contacted Fitbit customer service they suggested that I take the battery out and reinstall it.  That did the trick and I once again had a display on the front, but how often should I have to do that?  Then the tip of the silicone case fell off, exposing the sharp metal clip.  Once again I contacted customer service and they agreed to send me a new case.  Today it is not working again.  This time the Zip says on the display that I have 10,322 steps, my iPhone app says I have 7,099 steps, and the Fitbit website tells me I have 8,618.  Not very accurate to say the least.  My Zip has an icon of a battery with a line through it blinking on the front.  I have no idea what that means.  When I try to sync with my phone app it shows a full battery.  Since I have used it only month it certainly should be full.  I wish I had not been traveling when so much of this happened or I would have sent it back.  Just wasted money in my opinion.  I would not recommend any Fitbit product to anyone.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Zip Wireless Activity Tracker, Magenta

text_fidelity_a:
LUBAN 35 LB Adjustable Dumbbell and Kettlebell for Men and Women, Perfect for Home, Office, Gym Work Out I already had a Bowflex adjustable kettlebell that I liked a lot (though it's not perfect), but I wanted another adjustable kettlebell with lower weights for certain types of work. After four months of regular use, it's still in good shape and I'm glad I bought it.

Changing the plates is not as fast as on the Bowflex model, but it's easy, although the sliding tab sticks now and then. Still, it's fast enough for me to continue through a circuit without losing momentum, and that's what's important to me.

All the plates weight 2.5 lbs, and you can remove them however you like. That is, you don't have to take them from the top or the bottom. You will have to slot them back into the same place they came from, however, because they all curve in a certain way to give the kettlebell it's shape. The reviewer who mentioned sharp edges makes a good point, one worth considering for different exercises. For example, for swings it makes no difference to me where I pull the plates from, but if I'm doing shoulder presses, I pull them from the bottom or else I'll get my forearm unpleasantly poked and scraped as I use it. For a bottoms up carry, I find keeping the plates loaded at the top makes the weight more stable as I walk.

The plates make a slight rattle when swung -- that doesn't bother me, but it's something to keep in mind if working out within earshot of someone who might be disturbed by the noise. The plates do feel secure within the bell, but I still make it a habit to swing it so that the plates would fly away from me rather than at me if they came loose, and I swing them toward a wall or some other area where the plate wouldn't damage anyone. All that said, I'm sure I'm being overly cautious.

One thing I really like about this is the overall shape and footprint as compared to the Bowflex adjustable kettlebell. This one is a standard kettlebell size -- that makes it easier for me to handle, especially when it's in close to my body. The Bowflex is much larger, and that makes certain moves really awkward. It's not fair to compare these, though, given that they have very different weight ranges, but it's something I noticed. In those few places where the weights overlap, I almost always reach for this kettlebell over the Bowflex.

When buying exercise equipment, I'd much rather go to a shop where I can try it out in person and comparison shop. The pandemic made that impossible, so I crossed my fingers and hoped for the best. And it worked out. Even with its flaws, I've definitely gotten my money's worth for this.
text_fidelity_b: LUBAN 35 LB Adjustable Dumbbell and Kettlebell for Men and Women, Perfect for Home, Office, Gym Work Out

text_fidelity_a:
Cateye HL-1500 Gray Silver Halogen Headlight My review on HL 1500 is comparison against other models in this category which is, single unit(meaning no wire, no separate battery compartment), operates on regular batteries. If you are looking for a comparison to other type, specially high end models costing hundreds, this won't help.
Other models I had tried and some of them still in use are, Cateye HL500(2xC), Cateye EL500II MicroHalogen(4xAA), PlanetBike Super Spot 1W LED(4xAA). HL 500 and SuperShot are no longer in use because of not enough output. Super Spot 1W uses good plastic and good mechanical design, I wish it had more brightness. This made me convinced that LED stil has a long way to go, so I won't be trying another anytime soon.

Here's my review on HL 1500, mostly against MicroHalogen(HL500II).

Pros;
* Good illumination for its class about the same as HL500II Micro Halogen but has better pattern. 1W LED comes no where near this when it come to output. HL 1500 has wider(but not by much) more even with less waste outside area.
* It doesn't make ruttling noise as HL500II does while the bike is picking up the bumps. Sheets of sponge inside are probably helping the battery in place.
* Inexpensive, but I would pay a little more for the better material and construction.
* It works reasonably long time at more than 3 hrs per charge of NiMH. Since this is marketed mostly for commuting rider, 3 hrs. one way trip is highly unlikely. It's not marketed for 24 hr. race. If you know you are going to be riding in the dark more than 3 hrs. you can always carry a spare set of batteries or spare unit with batteies installed.
* It has two settings, high and low, where HL500II has only one which is the same as high on HL1500. Low setting maybe useful when riding in the city where you don't need much light but you need the drivers to know where you are.

Cons;
* It uses cheap plastic, all Cateye I had the same. It specially affects HL500II because the plastic parts are holding together against each other, this causes more stress to the plastic. On the other hand, HL1500 uses screw to hold the two plastic parts together. My HL500II already has cracks and about to come apart. Super Spot had thinner yet stronger plastic shell.
* It's bigger than HL500II. Not much of a problem but the space on the handle bar is limited. Smaller, the better.
* Not resistant to weather element, neither HL500II. HL1500 has only one rubber parts around the reflector housing, that's it.
* Replacing battery is not easy. You'll need a coin to screw and unscrew and the screw is hard to catch the nut at the other end. I wouldn't want to do it in the dark. Maybe better to have another unit with battery in, since it's not that expensive. On the other hand, HL500II doesn't use screw. It's going to be still hard in the dark but not as much as HL1500.

At the end, I prefer HL1500 over HL500II. I'm thinking getting another one, or maybe two.

*update*(Jan-15-10)
I ordered two more, this time from BikeWorldUSA(through Amazon but no longer available). It cost me less than $20.- for 2 units and shipping, can't beat the price. I got my first one from Cambria Bicycle Outlet. It's nice to have a spare unit with batteries already installed. My next question still remains, how long it'll take for the bulb to burn out.
I put a flat washer between the screw and the plastic body. There's nothing stopping the screw from chewing up the plastic.

*update*(Dec-22-10)
I took the HL-1500 to local bike shop and asked them to let me compare the brightness against other models, which they kindly accepted. Against EL-500(Cateye's second top of the line below EL-530 as one piece unit runs on 4 AAs). My HL-1500 was brighter than EL-500. According to spec sheet, HL-1500(3000 candlepower) still brighter than EL-530(1500 candlepower). It still needs side by side comparison to be confirmed though. EL-530(also 500) has longer burn time(90 hrs advertized) and LED will last nearly forever, so it has some advantage. But it costs $60.- compare to $10.- +S/H for HL-1500.
For those of you maybe interested in getting HL-1500, Cambria bicycle outfitter(where I bought the first one) still sell them.

*update*(Jun-14-11)
The bulb seems to be very long lasting, specially compare to MicroHalogen bulb which in my guess was about 200 to 300 hours and I went through a few of them. I use HL-1500 regularly and the one of three I use most get used about a few hours a week but the original bulb is still working. Very dependable.

*update* (1-25-16)
My current light in use since 2012.
http://www.amazon.com/gp/review/R1BNGTL2ZIZ93D?ref_=glimp_1rv_cl
text_fidelity_b: Cateye HL-1500 Gray Silver Halogen Headlight

Basically they are sending just SSSSS and not SOS like it should be, so no, it’s not a SOS, it’s just blinking with no information in it. It is what it is. I got them not for that, but to use as a lantern in our tent. Can’t speak about longevity yet and for how long fully charged battery would last. We will see. Three starts for today for missing real SOS and missing cord and wrap on one of them.

text_fidelity_a:
TETON Sports Celsius XXL Sleeping Bag; Great for Family Camping; Free Compression Sack After decades of backpacking with mummy sleeping bags, and never having enough warmth, we transitioned to 4WD tent camping. Although I never really minded the confines of a mummy bag my wife was never crazy about it so we looked for a bag with lots of space, width, and warmth. Weight and bag compression was no longer the primary criteria for purchasing a sleeping bag. That's good because this baby is relatively heavy and doesn't exactly pack small once taken out of the box, but that's fine for 4WD camping.

Experience has taught me that you want to purchase a sleeping bag that is rated at least 20 to 30 degrees colder than the coldest temperatures you expect to encounter. We occasionally camp in the mountains where night time temps drop into the high 20's and low 30's, but most of the time the night time temps are in the 40s to low 70s in a relatively dry Western-US environment, including the high desert. I was concerned we might overheat but my wife and I have remained comfortable across the entire temperature range wearing just a t-shirt and underwear or long underwear. She zips her bag up completely whenever the temps drop into the 40s or lower. I don't think I've zipped mine up completely yet.

We're no longer sleeping on a thin foam pad on the ground. We use these bags on cots with 3" thick foam pads. We both sleep like a rock. Our mummy bags have been handed down to our grown kids. As sleeping bags go, this one is a winner!
text_fidelity_b: TETON Sports Celsius XXL Sleeping Bag; Great for Family Camping; Free Compression Sack

text_fidelity_a:
CamelBak Flash Belt 17oz I wanted to like this belt because it is simple and lightweight, but it is expensive for what you get and I think there are a couple of important problems with the design. First, the main purpose of a hydration belt is to hold your water. This belt comes with an insulated water bottle, but the bottle is a non-standard size so you have to use their bottle. The bottle is narrower at the bottom than at the top, which helps you push it into its pocket. Unfortunately, no other bottles that I tried (including Camelbak bicycle water bottles) will fit (either the bottles are too wide or they fall out too easily).

Another problem is the single zippered pocket. The pocket will hold a phone up to about 6 inches tall. However, there is also a key ring in this pocket and I don't want my keys banging against my phone. I wish there was a smaller zippered pocket away from the phone pocket for keys. There is an open pocket on the other side that I assume if for holding energy gels.

The water bottle holds 17 ounces of water, which isn't that much, but that is usually plenty for me on a 1 hour run. Camelbak makes much larger hydration packs for hikers or mountain bikers that work well, but I am glad that have a lightweight option for joggers and runners. I just wish it was a little more functional and more competitively priced. There are lots of other runner hydration belts on the market.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Flash Belt 17oz

I like that there is a hook, that is also like a clip so I can clip it to a bag if necessary. I also really like that there is a lid for the the mouthpiece to keep it protected. It's been dropped a couple of times with no issues. I have only hand washed it, and so far no issues (only been a couple of weeks). It's cute, easy to carry, but when left in the car, it spits at me when I re-open it! A couple of other people have mentioned it on reviews as well. It's not worth me returning for that reason alone, but I would probably look elsewhere next time since there are so many other options.
Update - I've now had this a couple of months and traveled with it on an airplane. My old water bottles would occasionally "spit" from the pressure change on the plane, so I was fully ready (with my sleeve over the spout) to catch the water from this bottle. Oh, wow...it was like Niagara Falls! The funniest part was that the water ended up in my lap, so it looked like I just didn't make it to the rest room in time. I thought it was hilarious, but I can see how some would not. On the flight back, I just unscrewed the lid a tiny bit to release the pressure and no issues. The hook came in super handy when I wanted to clip it to the outside of my backpack.
The real reason I am updating my review is because it was hard to drink out of the straw due to the suction. As dumb as this sounds, I found myself drinking water less because of this issue. I went back and read some additional reviews and a couple people mentioned removing the little piece in the cap that effects the airflow. Eureka! It now works perfectly! I'll be using this bottle more often now.

text_fidelity_a:
Sawyer Products SP2129 Micro Squeeze Water Filtration System, 1 Pack, Black/Blue One thing you don't want to scrimp on is water filtering when you're hiking. Sawyer has an excellent reputation in the field, and we've used a different Sawyer filter for two years quite happily. This is a nice addition to their line-up.

Pros:
Size: it's small, compact, and quite light

Easy to use: screw it on to the included 32 0z. bladder once you've filled it, onto most regular types of disposable plastic water bottles (but please don't use those!), onto many bladders, or use the included straw to drink from the water source directly (though less comfortably). That's it.

Water flow: It comes out quickly enough to drink directly without any annoying pause or lag (you can also squeeze the bag for more flow).

Drinking bag feels quite durable, always a concern for these sorts of filters. I wouldn't be worried about this one.

Comes with an extra gasket, straw, and cleaning syringe

Backflushing is easy and quick

Quasi-negatives
Doesn't do viruses. I don't consider this a real negative since a) if you're hiking in the US you don't need to worry about viruses and b) if you're looking for something to take care of viruses you're looking for a real step up in price and product so that's a whole different category

No instructions. This is more just a little annoying, but easily solved by going online and looking at the videos.

It's a great little product from a trustworthy source. Water filters have come a long way from the old bulky pump action and so if you're still using one of those, consider moving up to something like this. So much easier and better to carry.
text_fidelity_b: Sawyer Products SP2129 Micro Squeeze Water Filtration System, 1 Pack, Black/Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Withings Pulse While I am only ten days into using my Withings Pulse Ox, I am very pleased with the purchase so far. Of all the devices currently on the market, this one seemed to offer the most bang for the buck. The step, activity, and sleep tracking seem to be quite accurate. The pulse and oxygen saturation monitoring are simple and precise. Battery life seems to be superb, and integration/connectivity with my iPhone have been no problem. Both the wristband and the belt clip are well-made and comfortable. I find that it really helps to motivate me to maintain and improve my health.

If I were to provide four pieces of constructive criticism they would be:
1) Make the Pulse OX waterproof or at least very water resistant.
2) Improve the Apple Healthkit Integration. I've had some issues, not in the Withings App, but within Healthkit, with doubling of steps.
3) Provide a means for background measurement of pulse and oxygen, rather than requiring the fingertip read. It is not practical to use for Zone Training or to see peak heart rate during a workout.
4) Allow for customization of the step and sleep goals.

Overall it has been a great little device though. Used in my "App Ecosystem" of the Withings App, WebMD, MapMyRun, and Healthkit...it is a nearly complete solution for my personal wellness goals.
text_fidelity_b: Withings Pulse

KastKing Sharky Baitfeeder III Spinning Reel 10+1 Shielded Stainless Steel BB - Carbon Fiber Drag for Live Liner Bait Fishing Action I don't write many reviews - typically when I do they are positive. I'm pretty disappointed. My wife bought me this this reel to go fishing with my kids for Father's Day. I had been reading about these Kastking bait feeders and it was much less expensive than a known Shimano. I watched some youtube videos about it that seemed pretty good and the amazon reviews seemed real good. We got to the pier and I had them spool it up with 20# mono. I like having my spools wound by the machine - it does a better job. The drag cap came off but it was difficult to remove. It seems like it took a good 2 minutes to unscrew... NOW it will not go back on - it freely spins and won't attach.
I posted a photo I can't tell if it's stripped or what is going on inside there. The threading appears to be fine.
The old timers that work at the pier fooled with it but said that's what I get for buying unknown name brands. I told them everyone started out unknown! I recently bought a penn battle II rod / reel combo and the rod was defective from the factory.
I wasted my $6 to get her spooled up with line but the worst part I didn't get to try out my new reel on father's day - I was really excited to use it! I'm glad I didn't get the other spool loaded up with braided line like I was thinking - I'd have been out another $30...
If the Kastking people make good on the replacement I'll test it out and will consider changing my rating. Right now I'm disappointed and wanted to gripe. Anticlimactic!
Is this rare or typical? We'll find out! Looking at other ratings seems like it might be rare (I hope). I'll update as things progress. - Wayne
text_fidelity_b: KastKing Sharky Baitfeeder III Spinning Reel 10+1 Shielded Stainless Steel BB - Carbon Fiber Drag for Live Liner Bait Fishing Action

text_fidelity_a:
Nordic Walking Poles for Individuals 6’ 2” – 6’ 3” = 132.5cm SWIX of Norway. All 32 Lengths Coming Soon 1-Piece Non-Collapsible. #1 for Hiking, Trekking, Physical Therapy. My review is primarily geared towards people who are interested in learning the Nordic walking techniques and are looking for inexpensive, appropriate walking sticks. It is also a comparison of the sticks offered here and the so-called “crappy Chinese” anti-shock, telescoping sticks. I have purchased both and am including photos below.

I started Nordic walking about 3 or 4 years ago. At the time, I wasn’t sure that this was something I would continue to do and did not want to spend a small fortune on equipment that would, once again, end up unused in a closet. But I was having trouble walking even a short distance (100 ft. or so) without excruciating burning in my legs and back, so thought I needed to give this a shot. I sprang for the cheap sticks and boy, am I glad I did! Within a few weeks, I was walking a mile with very little discomfort. That distance might be laughable to some, but to me, it was a miracle!

But honestly, it had less to do with the type of sticks than it did with learning the proper technique. There are many videos available that demonstrate the technique and anyone interested should spend some time watching them. It is not difficult to learn. In fact once you get the rhythm it’s like riding a bike…you don’t forget how to do it.

As far as the poles go, I see little difference in them. Perhaps at a higher price difference there is, but it’s still more about learning the skills.

Cheap Chinese poles (the black ones in the photos): When I bought mine I made some modifications. The rubber tips that were included wore out quickly. I replaced those with the boot type of tip which has lasted all these years and many miles. The tips are deeply grooved like snow tires and they do pick up small pieces of sand. This will make them slip some on asphalt, but it’s fairly easy to flick a grain of sand out and continue your walk. I also replaced the sponge rubber grip just below the handle (because it tore easily) with some closed cell tubing that I found online. That wasn’t entirely necessary because you never or rarely grab the poles in that area. I should have just eliminated it altogether.

These poles are the twist lock telescoping type (not the clamp type), which is handy when you don’t know what length pole you need in the beginning. But once adjusted, it is a PITA to collapse or readjust them. They do have a scale on them that shows the length you’ve set them to, so if you get these, make a note or find some way of marking the length. I never collapse mine anymore, because I want to start walking immediately, not fiddle with adjustments. However, if you need to pack your walking sticks, and don’t mind messing with the twist locks, this is certainly a consideration when you buy. I have never had the twist locks fail or accidently collapse once snuggly hand tightened.

These poles also have the anti-shock springs. It makes them heavier and, yes, they make a rattling noise every time the pole hits the pavement. Their extra weight does makes their footfall more forceful. I see no advantage to the springs at this point, but I’ve heard that they are helpful when going down steep terrain. Can’t say, because most of my walking is on fairly level pavement. BUT, DO NOT let the noise stop you from buying if you don’t want to spend a lot of money in the beginning. Getting you walking again is far more important than any minor rattles.

The handle grips are very comfortable and include a strap for your hands to go up through. I found these straps were much more comfortable for me and more convenient to use. Just remember to insert your hand up from the bottom of the strap.

Overall, these poles have a bigger diameter than the “real” ones and are slightly heavier. However, I think the few added ounces actually give you a better upper body and arm workout than the lighter poles. So, to me, the extra weight could be advantageous. Cost for these poles was 14.95 for each pole (@29.90). The Leki replacement tips cost $17.31 with tax, and I highly recommend them. I’m not including the rubber grip which is not necessary, so my actual cost was $47.21 with tax.

Real Nordic walking sticks (blue in the photos): As noted above, these are somewhat lighter, thinner, nonadjustable, non-spring-loaded poles. It is important that you order the right length. They adjustable have glove like straps attached to the handle.

Personally, I’m not entirely pleased with these particular straps. As you will see in the photos, their design leaves something to be desired. I have circled the points where they irritate my hands. And here, I will have to make some kind of modification if I want to use these poles for an extended time. The gloves interfere with wearing my fitness watch and the binding on some corners should be more rounded instead of squared off. Strapping your hand in or out, by means of Velcro strips, is awkward; and should you need to let go of your poles if you fall, you’re out of luck. There is a means of length adjustment (by pulling upward on the handle top) which is lacking in the Chinese poles, but it doesn’t solve the rubbing issues, since the part which cradles your hand doesn’t change position. After I have used these poles more, I may try to fashion a strap comparable to the ones on the Chinese poles.

The handles themselves are thinner and (though you shouldn’t be clasping them tightly) may be more suited to smaller hands. I can’t say for sure, but they are still comfortable.

I have a gut feeling that the boot tips on these sticks will wear quickly, needing to be replaced often. However, they do not have the deep tread of the Leki replacement tips and do not pick up grains of rock or sand, so that is an advantage as far as sliding on pavement goes. I will most likely replace these stock tips with the Leki ones and just deal with the rocks.

The cost for these poles (before any changes I may make) is, at this writing, $77.45 including tax and/or shipping. I am, otherwise, perfectly satisfied with these “real” Nordic walking sticks. They are light, not noisy and do what they’re supposed to do.

Both poles need some slight modification, but their functions are identical. Once again, it’s about technique, not one type of pole compared to another. Please do not let any hype make your decision. It’s far more important that you get out there and start walking.
I'm awarding 5 stars to either kind of pole. Both work pretty much equally.
text_fidelity_b: Nordic Walking Poles for Individuals 6’ 2” – 6’ 3” = 132.5cm SWIX of Norway. All 32 Lengths Coming Soon 1-Piece Non-Collapsible. #1 for Hiking, Trekking, Physical Therapy.

ARCEE Headlamp & Camping Lantern for Kids, Lightweight Portable Outdoor Indoor Tent Lamp for Children, Lanterns for Emergency, Hurricane, Power Outage, Nightlight for Kids’ Room Geared toward kids, yet anyone can benefit from it. Both the lantern and the headlamp come with preinstalled AA batteries, and CR2032 respectively. There is a spot in the description where it says "not included" but they are, and another that said they are. They are, can confirm. Just pull the little battery saver tab to activate. To access the battery compartment, you will need a tiny Phillips head screwdriver. Flat works too.

Both items are well made and durable feeling. I got that impression while unboxing. It just has a good feel, not cheap feeling. My video and pics are taken in a small dark storage room. Not actually producing colors.

The HEAD LAMP band is stretchy and adjustable. I was able to slide it onto y large 23.75" head. It is not something all that practical--no way to direct the light like one would with an adult sized head lamp but it is still useful. Good way to keep track of kid in darkness (camping, Halloween, emergency). It imparts a decent amount of direct light. I would even keep this in my car as a little emergency light. I could probably use this as a reading light if I wore it on my neck. Maybe.

TO OPERATE: press yellow button on top. THIS could be tricky for some kids and adults. As the pressure point location is directly in the convex center. Cant just press any spot on the yellow surface. Must be directly between eyes. Once that is figured out, then it is super easy.

The LANTERN is lightweight, yet robust feeling. Has TWO light options: top flashlight, forward direction. OR a diffuse lower lantern light. I think it lights up well enough for the space around. I am not sure why we would need to give a kid a spotlight (I just imagine little kiddos trying to blind others, This wont do that). I would use this myself in car, for sitting outside in evening, for light glow while walking around with dogs, or on my own, etc. I carry strong mag lights, but I find this little pack useful. Nice handle. Can be popped off if need be. Good base- wont easily tip over. Can take a drop to the ground, I think. Could hook this to a backpack and have lead adult or older kiddo to light up a path.

TO OPERATE: very easy, very intuitive, easy to press single button. Press to turn on upper flashlight, press again to switch it to the lantern. Another press simply turns it off.

I see they have an owl option and I love owls. My only choice was a frog. Frogs are cool, but owls are my love. I like this lantern enough to want to buy the owl for myself. I plan to keep the headlamp in my bag, and the lantern will just set out. I figured if the power goes out, it can't hurt to have extra options that don't require me to hold onto it. I can keep this on one of my end tables, and just press the button. Then I can use it to go get other supplies and such. Will make for a good glow, enough to light up area enough to be comfortable to maneuver.

----->>>>>>>In summary: This is a great little set. Fun looking, nice lights, COMES WITH BATTERIES INSTALLED, stretchy headband not limited to child use, good material, good feel, and is just refreshingly NICE product. Not cruddy feeling or looking. I do not rate on price, but I thought the full price reasonable. I bought the second one on sale (Prime Day), which was even better!

I recommend this for kids, for adults who still enjoy kid like stuff, for gift giving (I'll for practical gifts, and for a kid this would be fun and practical). They did well with including pre-installed batteries (just pull-out battery saver tag--if it doesn't fully come out, you will need to go in and take it out).

text_fidelity_a:
Penn International VIS 2 Speed Reel, Gold, 30 What a great reel for big, powerful fish! If you target fish that measure in the hundreds of pounds, and you want the best tool for the job, this is your reel. In my case, it's the reel I use when we go deep for big halibut here in Alaska. This reel holds plenty of line to get to those shelves 400 feet down where the barndoors lie, with plenty of line left over to allow for long runs that those big fish make. If you hang up and break off, losing several hundred feet of line (it happens), you don't have to hang it up because the reel holds enough line to let you keep fishing.

I like the high-speed retrieve for pulling up from the deep when you need to check your bait or try something else. When you latch into a fish, though, a quick push of the button on the hub of the handle engages the more powerful lower gears, so you can really torque into the fish.

That new handle design is nice, too. It comfortably fits my hand, has a nice rubbery, no-slip texture, and helps spread the stress across the meaty part of my hand so long battles are just a little bit easier.

The open design of the "X" series frame (with no crossbars across the front of the spool) is helpful when there's a backlash to deal with (yeah, it still happens once in a while). These reels aren't cheap, but they're the best you can buy. Solid, reliable, and made in USA. No regrets here!

Let me know if you don't anything in my review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Penn International VIS 2 Speed Reel, Gold, 30

Features Disc-Style U-Locks with 2 Keys (4"/102mm Wide, 8"/203mm Long) I commute by bike, and I have to carry my bike up and down a flight of stairs 5 days a week. My bike is an e-bike that weighs 50 lbs without any gear attached. After adding a rack, trunk bag, lights, etc., it's probably up to 60 lbs. The bike is fairly expensive, and I work on a university campus, so I need a lock I can rely on. I originally purchased the [[ASIN:B005VMO49U Abus Bordo GRANIT X Plus 6500/85cm (33.46 in) black - Folding lock, Bike lock, Security level 15]] because of it's high security rating. Now I have this lock. I love this lock! It's so light! It barely adds any weight to bike. It's also easy to lock. I like that I can remove the barrel, position the lock, and then replace and lock the barrel without the key. The security rating on this isn't as high as the ABUS, but I see so few of these in the wild that I don't think your average bike thieves are prepared to break this lock. At least I hope not.

As an added bonus, my e-bike has a cage mount on it's battery, and that's where I've attached this lock. So when I remove the battery to charge it, this lock serves as a very welcome handle for the rather heavy battery. :)

As far as I know, no one's tried to break my lock yet, so I can't say for certain how secure it is. But it has a good rating, it feels secure, and it's light and easy to use. So I'm happy.

text_fidelity_a: SABRE Personal Safety Kit With Pepper Spray and Personal Alarm, 25 Bursts, Intuitive Finger Grip, 120dB Alarm, Audible Up To 1,280-Feet (390-Meters) I have never used any type of pepper spray or personal safety items. I thought it might give some peace of mind during some situations. The items are two separate devices, so there are two things to keep track of. Ideally, it would be great if they were combined somehow into one device. Both items have a key chain attachment so you can keep it with your keys. I have put them on a lanyard instead though, for fear of accidently setting them off. I keep the lanyard inside the outer pocket of my purse. I can also wear the lanyard around my neck if desired. I was afraid to test these items, but I did. To activate the alarm, you pull the pin with the key chain. Once it's removed, a loud, piercing sound is made. It frightened the cats immediately! It wasn't too loud that it hurts your ears. It kind of reminded me of a car alarm sound. The alarm stops when you reinsert the pin and click it in place.  My husband and I tested the pepper spray outside. It was a windy day, so we made sure that we didn't spray it against the wind. A reddish orange stream of pepper spray was dispensed. The description of the product says it goes about 10 feet. We didn't measure it, but that seems pretty close to what we got. I like that you get about 25 sprays from it. I did get some on my finger. It dripped down from the dispenser. I immediately wiped my hand on the grass, then went inside and washed it thoroughly.  I was able to get it off because it didn't burn or sting. It doesn't have much of a smell. Hopefully, I won't have to use these! There is an expiration date on the pepper spray which is good to know.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Personal Safety Kit With Pepper Spray and Personal Alarm, 25 Bursts, Intuitive Finger Grip, 120dB Alarm, Audible Up To 1,280-Feet (390-Meters)

I ordered it because it is quite similar to an REI one that my son has and my grandson loved. But when it arrived I noticed I'd inadvertently ordered the XL with a 300 lb weight capacity and was afraid it'd be way too big. But it's actually about the width of your standard folding camp chair and the size easily accommodates someone half that weight without feeling like overkill. The bulk of the chair is made with strong weatherproof ripstop fabric. The sides are a sturdy fine mesh. The stitching is even and flawless with reinforcement at the pressure points. There are pull loops to assist with inserting the aluminum legs. There is a handy stretchy pocket beneath the seat for cellphones, keys or whatever. The overall design is sleek and attractive with a very nice Timber Ridge logo stitched into the seat back. This chair sits low to the ground, low enough to easily set a drink on the ground and reach for it when desired.  It has a sling like seat that is very comfortable and lends itself well to a "laid back" posture with locked fingers cupped behind the head. When sitting, this chair will not feel as stable as the standard 4 legged camping chair. But it does feel every bit as stable as other backpacking chairs of this design. It is easy to assemble (with the slight exception of inserting the final leg into it's corresponding pocket) and disassemble. It packs up into a duffle slightly larger than a loaf of bread. Unbelievably, it weighs less than 2.5 lbs. I highly recommend this chair if you need a smaller profile chair for backpacking, or just to save packing space when camping (packed, it is 1/3 the size of standard camping chairs), or storing in a vehicle. The price is very competitive.

Sportline Lightweight Walking Advantage 385 Tally Counter With Easy To Read Number Display That Counts Up To 9999 Anyone working out on an indoor track will find a counter helpful. At 12 laps a mile, counting laps is difficult. Counting is easy; remembering how many laps I've done is hard.

The Sportline counter fixes what my math teacher could not, allowing me to turn my mental energies toward my workout, or toward a conversation with my running partner.

---Necessary on a Practical Level---
I tried a system of using my fingers on my right hand to measure laps 1-5, then using my left hand to measure how many laps in groups of five. That is, two fingers on my left and three fingers on my right would equal 13 laps. It sounds easier to employ than it actually is.

The Sportline counter has five worthwhile features:
* It counts one per click, up to 9,999. I won't run more than that, so, for me, it is plenty.
* The display is legible while running. The white digits are large, on a black background.
* The size of the device is small enough to carry.
* The finger loop fits nicely in my middle finger.
* The reset dial quickly zeroes out the counter.

The only two drawbacks are
* The reset dial would be more comfortably located on the left, not the right side of the counter, or otherwise better engineered for right-handed users.
* The weight is heavy. It is small, but can feel like baggage during a longer workout.

The Sportline counter is sturdy, does as advertised, and serves well as a tool for anyone walking or running a lot of laps.

Anthony Trendl
[...]
text_fidelity_b: Sportline Lightweight Walking Advantage 385 Tally Counter With Easy To Read Number Display That Counts Up To 9999

Dynaplug Racer Pro Bicycle Tire Repair Tool 100% USA Made (Orange) I did the Unbound Gravel 200 and, like many others during the race, got a flat tire. The sharp Flint Hills rock sliced about a 3/8 in cut in my sidewall around 45 miles in. I run inserts in my tubeless tire setup, so I really didn’t want to have to put a tube in because (1) it is really hard to get the tire off and (2) I didn’t want to have to carry the sealant covered insert 30 miles until the next checkpoint.

I wasn’t sure if the Dynaplug would get the tire to seal or how long it would hold due to the size of the cut. I’ve had smaller sidewall cuts that regular bacon strips couldn’t fix. After using 2 plugs and spinning the wheel on its side a few times, I was very pleased to see the tire held air - and it held for the next 155 miles to the finish.

I highly recommend Dynaplug and especially the Racer Pro model that holds 4 plugs. I wouldn’t want to go on any epic rides with any lesser tool. It is on the expensive side, but it is worth the peace of mind and ease of use.

My area is abutted by Army Corp of Engineer "wild" land that goes (about a quarter of a mile) to a large lake not far from my house.  Just this past week my neighbor and I spotted a bobcat in the wild land back there!  We have coyotes, wild boars, raccoons, opossums, armadillos and a few other critters we've seen and documented.  This laser range finder has allowed me to get an idea of how close some of the wild life is getting to my yard.  I have small dogs and the coyotes worry me more than most of the other critters.  So when I spot one slinking around the edge of the woods, I grab this range finder and document when, where and how far they were from me.  At some point, if they get to be a bit too bold, the neighbors and I will have to report the pack as being dangerous.  Having documented the times, the places and how far they were from me, a human, will be helpful in proving that they need to be trapped and moved or dealt with in some other way.  I know this range finder is good for golf or even hunting - I guess my use is more akin to hunting, but I will say that it is easy to use, sighting in on the critter to find the distance.  That's what I need to know!

Reliance Products Aqua-Tainer 7 Gallon Rigid Water Container (Pack of 2) I've owned this brand and style of water container for almost 17 years, it's my go-to for camping and day trips where there might not be any water. I have almost always had at least 2 of them, one for drinking water, the other for potable water (cleaning dishes, cooking, dog water). Recently having to purchase two more, I guess the one that's put on the age and seen places finally developed a crack on the bottom. Not bad after 7-8 years being lugged around.

Pros: Lots of water on hand - Easy to use - Stack able - Durable - Trusted brand -

Cons: Heavy once full (7gallons x 7lbs per gallon of water + container = 50lbs) - spigot almost never lines up pointing down no matter how many ways you screw on the cap - price raised by $10 in past year

Points to look at when choosing: If you can't lift 7 gallons, get the 2.5 or 5 gallon model
(Here is an example per the National Park Service) 2 gallons a day per person when camping, you can figure the same if the water at your house is shut off during a emergency event. You might add an extra gallon for toilet flushes.

text_fidelity_a:
The Firm TransFIRMer The FIRM Supercharged Sculpting workout is a highly stylized workout with electronica, artistically designed sets and a clean, sleek mood. This is a combination of traditional weight training with aerobics using the necessary TransFIRMer. Most of the exercises are recognizable as traditional exercises like plank or sit-ups and squats.

The lunges seem easier to do with the TransFIRMer, although weights are used throughout most of the exercises to give them a little more edge. The workout is followed by a brief stretching segment, but if you want to totally relax, there is a "Bonus: 8-minute Stretch Workout."

This set also includes two additional DVDs: The FIRM Ultimate Calorie Blaster and The FIRM Aerobic Body Shaping. If you have any issues with your knees, you may need to try various workouts to see which ones you can manage. I found the Ultimate Calorie Blaster DVD was hard on the knees.

"The TransFIRMer was designed with multiple uses in mind and has 5 different configurations to take each workout to the next level." ~ pg. 6

The TransFIRMer can be positioned in five different ways to increase the possibilities:

6" TransFIRMer - The green section can be used alone
8" TransFIRMer - The blue section can be used alone
14" TransFIRMer - The blue and green sections used together
Side-by-Side TransFIRMer - The blue and green sections placed next to each other
Incline TransFIRMer - The green piece fits into the blue piece for a convenient and stable incline.

"You can adjust the intensity of the workout depending on how high you step." ~ pg. 7

The workout booklet has some interesting rotation calendars so you can plan out 21 days. There is also a section on healthy eating tips, an eating plan, 21-day diet plan, list of 100-calorie snacks and list of 200-calorie snacks. A substitution list makes the diet easier to follow especially if you are eating out and want to still keep to the diet plan.

For years I couldn't do the FIRM workouts because I kept forgetting to buy the equipment, but now with the step at home I can try out most of the new workouts and have fun working out. The 2-piece step is also easy to arrange and is very sturdy. The low-impact exercises work well with the step and the incline is used for push-ups, cardio, arms and ab exercises. If you are buying this step to also use with other workouts that use a step, they say that is not recommended.

~The Rebecca Review
text_fidelity_b: The Firm TransFIRMer

text_fidelity_a:
EVERCROSS Electric Scooter, 500W/350W Motor & 10" /8" Solid Tires, 20-22 Miles Range &19 Mph, 3 Speed Modes, Folding Commuter Electric Scooter for Adults Teenagers [[VIDEOID:7c963067c4b7ab3cf11ca74bdcaddaa3]] So my wife loves roller blading and after trying it a number of years back, we discover it is NOT my cup of tea. For all the things I can do, that is NOT one of them. So I miss out when she goes... and I started to see these eScooters and thought... why not? Had the chance to get one a couple of weeks ago, but then had the chance to get this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter and grabbed it. We like both - and now we can each have one for things other than her blading. Each has a couple "cons," but nothing we can't get over or around. And in the end, we really like them - both. But... I think I actually like this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter slightly more... here's our take:

1. It comes in a perfect box - meaning the packing and all was great for taking care of the EVERCROSS Electric Scooter while inside and throughout delivery. It is also great for gifting - the recipient will open it up to find... a fully put together scooter. The ONLY things you have to do: pull up and pop into place the front stick and handle bars and adjust the height of the handle bars. Both totally easy. There is literally NOTHING to assemble. You are only adjusting the handle bars to a comfortable height and it's totally easy. And you are popping that front stick with the handle bars because this thing is collapsable.

2. I repeat, it is collapsable. That means you can take it almost anywhere. If I had had this back in college... life would have been easier! You can literally break that front stick and bars down, and put them into the INCLUDED BAG that lets you carry this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter anywhere. Think about the student in your life! That huge campus! Or how about that "commute" in your city or town and then NOT wanting to leave the eScooter outside! This bag is well built, with solid materials and lets you take this thing anywhere! Oh where were you in college...

3 We got out there and tested - my wife on the first one, me on this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter. One of the reasons I do like this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter a little better is that i's weight limit is slightly higher that the other one. That means the weight I recently put on due to an illness does not keep me off of it until I get the weight back off - I'm out there now, not in a few weeks!

It is smooth, easy to ride, and you are up and going within minutes of getting it out of the box! The instructions feel a little intense - a lot to pick up and know, mostly around the box with all the information you're given while riding (mph, what level you are at, etc). I'm part of the way through, but I wanted to ride - so out we went. I can ride a SEGWAY with ease - when you get on this you'll understand that comparison - as this is about balance and the like. For we of GenX, (think skateboards and roller blades - neither I was great at) the SEGWAY was something I could master. So this eScooter I thought I was also in a good position to take on, and I was right. Balance is there, eases of use, turning, stopping... all there. Kids today... they'll rock this thing quickly.

4. Breaking. This is another point for the EVERCROSS Electric Scooter. The other one we have will stop on a dime! I mean, you hit the breaks and according to my wife, you STOP. That IS great for certain situations - and like this in reverse - you simply have to get used to it. (like driving a car). BUT, on the EVERCROSS Electric Scooter the breaks act more like a slowing device ... not a STOPPING one!
You hit them and SLOW down, NOT STOP. I like this from the standpoint that I feel as I have more OVERALL control as I am riding AND stopping. For me this is a plus. For someone else, they/you might prefer the STOP of that break system. My wife thinks she likes this slowing option better (and at some point we will be able to switch and she can use this while I try that), but for now, this is mine (maybe I won't take off that weight... ). Again, this slowing type stop means I can control the stop, the turns, and maneuvering while NOT stopping outright, but when I need to stop, I bring it down in speed, then you step off to stop. So far it has NOT been a problem and actually, again, I really like it.

5. There is a GREAT light! Do not let your wife, child, or anyone else "Test" it while you are looking directly into it!

6. There is an "emergency break" in that you can step on the back fender to STOP it - read the instructions. Apparently you DO NOT want to do this often or you'll wear out the tire.

7. The tires are great! I have ridden around our community and over bumps, "flat" speed bumps, those lines that are always painted with slick paint (motorcycle riders get it), and leaves and twigs... so far it's been great and I feel safe and in control. Fastest I've gone: 10 mph. We live in a community with kids and cars, so until I can get somewhere I can open it up... but so far so great and I'm having fun!

8. That weight thing... Check your weight and what it can handle. I did put on a few pounds and until I get those off and back to moving down, I cannot use the other eScooter. But this one I was fine within the limits. Which made me wonder, because this eScooter is actually slightly smaller overall. Including the wheels. So... why? No worries, I can still use this and it moves. I have gone up and down hills here in the area fine - we are NOT talking about LARGE hills, but enough that with my weight I should have noticed any issues and did not. It never felt like it was working any harder.

9. And once you get comfortable, there is a readout box on the handle bars you can track things like mph and the like. There are (I think my wife said) three speed levels - we quickly moved me up to #2. I am very comfortable at this level and should not take long to try out and use #3 - again, I am very comfortable on a SEGWAY, and again, this is important as the concept of balance and speed are very similar. The box is easy to read, though I've not even tried to change anything while riding and my wife being the one to read the instructions, made adjustments when we'd stop. I THINK this is how it is set up - to only adjust on a stop, but do not quote me on that. When making said adjustments, it's easy to use and to see. I am again, GenX with a need for reading glasses when... reading. BUT I did not need them to see perfectly fine and clearly the printouts on the box.

10. The handlebars... are good. This is another SLIGHT "con" in that they do "SHAKE" while you are riding. In order to fold up and then go down with the front stick in order to pack it away, they are bendable. HOWEVER, that means in the locked position there IS a noticeable shake or wobble to them. I REALLY noticed it at first and it did "shake my confidence," BUT I quickly got used to them and was fine. It is something my wife said, as she tried it, that it made her uncomfortable and it was one thing she put in the WIN column for the other eScooter. SO... it'll be a personal preference.

11. There is a kickstand to keep it up on its own. Well designed and easy to use!

12. SIZE MATTERS... Or does it?
We both agree the other eScooter IS bigger... platform, height, wheels, but... we also both agree, it doesn't much matter. I have put on that weight, I do not fit into the other one's weight limit, but I do on this smaller one... so.... does size matter? For weight, apparently not. FOR COMFORT... I did have to try a couple positions to decide how I felt I fit best on the PLATFORM. When standing you are likely not going to be standing front to back, but facing to one side or the other - this appears to be common on the eScooters we have seen. Okay, no worries... and I tried one direction (left) and was not at all comfortable. Flipped myself to the right and all was great! I fit - BUT I also notice I am in a smaller space than the other eScooter... but it honestly was not a problem for me. BUT a larger (read taller) person might find the shortness of the deck uncomfortable.

Overall, we LOVE this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter and are THRILLED to have it! Whether we take turns and switch off, this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter is a welcome addition for my wife and I. I'll be able to go with her when she blades or we can each take one and have time out. We have NOT had to recharge yet - we haven't been far enough yet to need it - so I cannot yet speak to that process. If it is anything but great, I'll come back to UPDATE. But we are expecting it to be as easy as the rest of our experience with this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter. In the end, would I pick one or the other?????? Ad of right now... yes, I think I would pick this EVERCROSS Electric Scooter over the other - for me. I 1. like the slowing of the breaks, 2. that it takes my weight - even when I loose it I like that idea, 3. that it fully and easily breaks down and goes into the included bag. BUT that does not mean the other eScooter does not have great elements to it. In the end... as far as THIS EVERCROSS Electric Scooter how do we like it? WE LOVE IT! This is a great eScooter for adults!
text_fidelity_b: EVERCROSS Electric Scooter, 500W/350W Motor & 10" /8" Solid Tires, 20-22 Miles Range &19 Mph, 3 Speed Modes, Folding Commuter Electric Scooter for Adults Teenagers

Dynamic Discs Cadet Disc Golf Bag | Introductory Disc Golf Bag | Great for Beginners and Casual Disc Golf Rounds | Lightweight and Durable Frisbee Golf Bag | 10-12 Disc Capacity… My first bag, and I still use it. It holds ten discs easily, although more putters makes it tight (I carry two putters). It is great for those of us who don't want to carry more than 10 discs. The Midnight Blue color looks very nice. The small size of the bag means that it is prone to tipping over on uneven ground, but the discs usually stay put. Because of the lack of other pockets, I typically use the putter pocket for a towel.

The mesh pocket inside the top is unusable when not playing. The height of the discs makes it difficult to close the top, so anything stored in the top will interfere with closing. During play you leave the top unzipped, so you could keep a towel or marker disc in it during the game.

The bottle pocket holds a standard plastic water bottle, but anything bigger is very tight or too big. There is no tie for the beverage holder, so your bottle may fall out if the bag tips over.

Despite these drawbacks, I do recommend this bag for it's small size.

Dynamic Discs: If you come out with a redesign, I'd buy another if it has these improvements. Those of us who prefer to carry fewer discs still need some of the features found on larger bags.
- Ability to hold a larger water bottle would be nice.
- A full-width/full-height pocket for a towel and/or golden disc retriever on the back would be very nice.
- A marker disc pocket on the front of the putter pocket would be nice.
- A small pocket on the opposite end of the bottle holder would be nice.
text_fidelity_b: Dynamic Discs Cadet Disc Golf Bag | Introductory Disc Golf Bag | Great for Beginners and Casual Disc Golf Rounds | Lightweight and Durable Frisbee Golf Bag | 10-12 Disc Capacity…

text_fidelity_a:
GardePro E2 Trail Game Camera, 16MP 1080P, Wide 110° View Angle, 75ft Night Vision, 0.5S Motion Activated for Game Wildlife Deer Trail [[VIDEOID:14a484a2d74d598d71a2b96fca9961c2]] I was trying to wait and get some fantastic footage before I posted a review ... but that did not happen. Mostly our own cats, possums, raccoons, boring stuff.

Let me back up by saying we have used game cameras for years. I have purchased a handful of bum cameras from cheap foreign made cameras to US made well known cameras. I appreciate a good camera. I have had some just stop working and some get struck by lightning. We live on 24 woody acres and personally ... I like to see what goes bump in the night and during the day. We have caught bobcats, coyotes, deer, and wild pigs on our cameras. Still waiting for that Cougar.

Easy to set. Doesn't seem to drain batteries easily. I like that I can choose .avi or .mov files. I tend to use .mov files because I use an iPhone and an iMac ... so easier for me. This is actually the only camera I have bought that does that. Sensitive. Seems to catch the baby possums way in the background easy.

Fishing On The Fly | Fly Fishing Reel | High-Grade Aluminum Alloy | 3/4, 5/6, 7/8 Weights | Black I ordered this Fishing on the Fly reel for a couple of reasons. The reel I keep my sinking line on took a dump last time I was on the water, and I needed something to replace it. I went with this because of its clicking on retrieve (my preference), it's design, and of course, its price.
It reviewed well, and I figured that even if half of what people said were true, it would be a decent reel for the "price" as people always say.
This isn't just a decent reel "at the price"; it's a nice reel. It would be a nice reel at twice the price, and perhaps even at 2.5x the price. I used to work at a big box Outfitter outlet with a tin green roof, and this EXACT reel, with a better known branding and packaging, sold for more than twice the price. And I sold a lot of them.

The reel is tight, tolerances are close, setting the drag is positive and tactile, and it's light yet sturdy feeling. It handles fish very well, and stripping line out feels good.

I like the packaging, I love the little felt reel bag, and there's a form letter from the company owner that makes it sound like he is rely interested in the customer being happy with the product. And even though the reel is made in China, the literature included is in English. Proper English that wasn't just run through Google Translate. If I were to have an issue with this reel (which I don't foresee), I get the impression he would want to make it right.

My wife bought this reel for me, so even though this isn't a "confirmed purchase" out whatever it's called, we did pay for this, and I'm glad we did!

Basically stated, I like this reel a lot. I'll buy another one. The only thing I'd like to see is other color options. That's really the only complaint I'd want to see addressed in a reel of this build quality at anywhere below $90. You can't go wrong picking one of these up!
text_fidelity_b: Fishing On The Fly | Fly Fishing Reel | High-Grade Aluminum Alloy | 3/4, 5/6, 7/8 Weights | Black

I think it would work very well for a teacher, college professor, or a graduate student to use to carry a small laptop, a tablet, folders and papers in. This bag might also be perfect for realtors or insurance salesmen, and it's a nice size to use as a carry on bag when travelling as well.

Measuring 17.7" long x 12.6" high x 7.9" wide, this bag is made of sturdy water resistant canvas with genuine leather trim and stainless steel hardware. The bag has webbed leather trimmed carry handles plus a detachable adjustable strap so it can be carried by hand, as a shoulder bag, or cross body. The brown bag's color is true to the picture shown in the product description and the leather trim, handles, carry strap, and interior lining are done in a darker brown color that provides an attractive contrast.

While most of the bag's storage area is within the roomy main compartment, there are also several storage areas on the outside as well. The front and back of the bag each has a 14" long by 8.5" high zippered compartment which is plenty large enough to carry travel papers, small tablets, or other gear you want ready access to, and there are large 6.5" x 6.5" snap closing sleeves on each end of the bag to hold beverages or other gear.

The zippered main compartment is fully lined in a dark cocoa brown colored cotton fabric which will conceal ink marks or other stains nicely. One side of the compartment has an 8" x 5" zippered compartment, and the other has a well padded 15" long laptop sleeve. I tried to fit my 15" Lenovo Thinkpad into the sleeve but it was too tight, so I think you'll be fine with a 13" or 14" laptop but not a larger one. The laptop did fit into the main compartment itself with room to spare, so you could always use the padded sleeve for a tablet and still take your laptop along.

Stitching throughout this bag is straight and even, and everything is reinforced at stress points. Zippers are well sewn in and all open and closed smoothly. This is a very well made bag made of durable materials. As it can fit everything from a 15" laptop in the center plus folders, or a 14" laptop plus iPad in addition to some books and folders in the center, I think this would make a sturdy book bag, briefcase bag, or travel bag.

Advanced Food Journal for Women & Men - Perfect Food Diary for Tracking Your Daily Nutrition & Weight Loss - Body Measuring Tape Included w/Planner - Diet Journal for Weightloss & Meal Tracking My wife and I are working on a healthier overall lifestyle and as we get going again we are doing it with charting in a journal this time. I had found one a while back and love it, but was looking for one for my wife. Another was very basic and beginner. So... when I saw this Advanced Fitness Journal for Women & Men I grabbed it and thrilled I did. It is very similar to mine and offers her the main points we both look for. It’s well done and well laid out, and it’s going to be a great asset for her.

The Advanced Fitness Journal for Women & Men arrives with a body measuring tape. Mine did as well and I was very impressed with that - if you’re going to chart your weight and body size, having a body soft measuring tape is a must - but often these journals do not include them. Why? NO clue... so when this Advanced Fitness Journal for Women & Men arrived with one I was thrilled.

The Advanced Fitness Journal for Women & Men is laid out very well. The covers are done well for protecting and letting you work in the journal, the spirals are strong and let you lay it out flat to write in, so from the start it’s perfect - you can work well and easily in it.

The pages are laid out well, with all the facts you are wanting to keep track of, from size to body parts as you start and at intervals along the way. I love that it includes tips on how and where to take these as well - something mine doesn’t do. But in this case, not only, that, but it looks nicely laid out ad easy to use. Impressive.

There are other tips such as how to develop muscle. This is helpful and encouraging and a well done addition.

Where I am very happy - as is my wife - is about the workouts themselves. I have seen journals that are done in ways that show the person(s) writing them have no idea what working out includes or how it is done. NO idea what that sets and reps are different from the actual exercise. I walk away scratching my head. But not here. M48 Tactical Tomahawk Military Axe - Green/Black with Compass & Sheath | 3 ⅞” Cast Stainless Steel Axe | Piercing Spike | Nylon Cord Wrapped Fiberglass Handle | Camping and Tactical Gear | 15” Length I collect knives and hawks. There are two ways that I judge the effectiveness of any sharp tool. Number One is how it stacks up to a good machete. At this point if I could only take one blade into the wilderness, it would be a high quality machete. It has reach and a long cutting surface, is fundamental in design, and can create a large protected area around the user. In addition it cuts through things easily and doesn't typically get hung up in/on the target, unlike other implements. Number Two is judging how I would feel if I were threatened with the tool. It does look wicked, it has two effective blades, it comes sharp(!), can be swung in any direction, and is well built. It's inherent light weight will allow a lot of use before arm fatigue sets in, but it does have some negatives.

On the con side, it is short and its lightness doesn't make it feel substantial in my hand. The cutting surface is much smaller than that of a good machete and of course you can't really stab with it. It is a swinging tool that will allow an experienced fighter to step inside of the swing. Although I haven't tested it, it's hard for me to believe that it can stand up to the abuse that a large man can generate. The M48 probably wouldn't last long against a hard target (breaching doors or cutting wood or metal) but it should prove to be easy to carry and extremely effective against a soft target. I certainly wouldn't want to be hit with it. The best part of the M48 is the value. It is simply one of the most cost effective blades that I have ever bought. And darn, it just looks and feels cool!
text_fidelity_b: M48 Tactical Tomahawk Military Axe - Green/Black with Compass & Sheath | 3 ⅞” Cast Stainless Steel Axe | Piercing Spike | Nylon Cord Wrapped Fiberglass Handle | Camping and Tactical Gear | 15” Length
